title: Modes of Inheritance & Imprinting Syndromes
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: Modes of Inheritance

changelog.change: Initial entry — Mendelian pattern table with recurrence risk and examples, plus selected imprinting / microdeletion syndromes.

purpose: Quick reference for counselling recurrence risk by inheritance pattern, and for the imprinting and microdeletion syndromes whose parent-of-origin matters (Prader-Willi vs Angelman are the same 15q region, opposite parent).

rows: Autosomal dominant
50% if one parent affected (allow for variable expressivity, incomplete penetrance, and new mutations — e.g. ~ 80% of achondroplasia is de novo)
Achondroplasia, Marfan syndrome, neurofibromatosis 1, Huntington disease
Autosomal recessive
25% if both parents are carriers; carrier frequency rises with consanguinity
Cystic fibrosis, galactosaemia, phenylketonuria, sickle cell disease, most inborn errors of metabolism
X-linked recessive
~ 50% of the sons of a carrier mother are affected; daughters are usually unaffected carriers; no male-to-male transmission
Haemophilia A/B, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, G6PD deficiency
X-linked dominant
Affected in both sexes; often more severe or lethal in males
X-linked hypophosphataemic rickets; Rett syndrome (with male lethality)
Mitochondrial
Maternal transmission only; heteroplasmy → variable expression
MELAS, MERRF, Leber hereditary optic neuropathy
Prader-Willi
Loss of the PATERNAL 15q11–q13 (deletion or maternal uniparental disomy)
Neonatal hypotonia and poor feeding → later hyperphagia, obesity, short stature, hypogonadism, learning disability
Angelman
Loss of the MATERNAL 15q11–q13 (same region, opposite parent)
Severe intellectual disability, seizures, ataxic 'puppet' gait, inappropriate laughter, minimal speech
Beckwith-Wiedemann
11p15 imprinting defect
Macrosomia, macroglossia, omphalocele / abdominal-wall defect, neonatal hypoglycaemia (hyperinsulinism), hemihyperplasia; increased Wilms tumour and hepatoblastoma risk — tumour surveillance
Williams
7q11.23 microdeletion (includes ELN)
Supravalvular aortic stenosis, 'elfin' facies, infantile hypercalcaemia, an over-friendly / 'cocktail-party' personality, intellectual disability
Noonan (a RASopathy)
Autosomal dominant (PTPN11 and others)
Short stature, webbed neck, pulmonary valve stenosis / hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, pectus, bleeding diathesis — 'Turner-like' but normal karyotype and occurs in both sexes
22q11.2 deletion (DiGeorge / velocardiofacial)
22q11.2 microdeletion
Conotruncal cardiac defects, hypocalcaemia (hypoparathyroidism), thymic hypoplasia / T-cell immunodeficiency, cleft palate, learning and psychiatric problems

body.text: When a genetic syndrome is suspected, chromosomal microarray is the first-line test for intellectual disability / multiple anomalies (detects copy-number changes a karyotype misses). Methylation studies for Prader-Willi/Angelman/Beckwith-Wiedemann; targeted gene panels or exome sequencing when the phenotype is non-specific.

buildNote: Counselling reference — recurrence risk by pattern + the parent-of-origin imprinting syndromes.
